{{For|others of a similar name|David Brown (disambiguation){{!}}David Brown}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''David Anthony Brown''', {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS|FBPhS}} (10 February 1936 — 21 October 2023)<ref>{{cite web |last1=Page |first1=Clive |title=In memoriam: Professor David Brown {{!}} British Pharmacological Society |url=https://www.bps.ac.uk/news/articles/2023/in-memoriam-professor-david-brown |website=www.bps.ac.uk |access-date=1 November 2023}}</ref> was a British pharmacologist. He was emeritus Professor  of [[Pharmacology]] at [[University College London]], having joined the department in April 1987 and served as Head of Department from October 1987 to April 2002.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/david-brown-11146/|title=David Brown &#124; Royal Society|website=royalsociety.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=David A. Brown Lab|url=http://www.ucl.ac.uk/npp/research/dab|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120229022249/http://www.ucl.ac.uk/npp/research/dab|url-status=dead|archive-date=29 February 2012|publisher=University College London|accessdate=14 March 2013}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=David Brown - Faculty Profile at University College London website |url=https://iris.ucl.ac.uk/iris/browse/profile?upi=DABRO00 |access-date=8 June 2022}}</ref> He is known for the discovery of the [[M current]] in the 1970s.
 
==Education==
Brown graduated from University College with a BSc degree in [[Chemistry]], [[Zoology]] and [[Physiology]], followed by Special Physiology, and from [[St Bartholomew's Hospital Medical College]] with a PhD in pharmacology.

==Career and research==
Prior to joining UCL Brown was Wellcome Professor of Pharmacology at the [[School of Pharmacy, University of London|School of Pharmacy]]. He also held [[visiting professor]]ships in the Universities of [[University of Chicago|Chicago]], [[University of Iowa|Iowa]] and [[University of Texas|Texas]], and the [[Kanazawa University|University of Kanazawa]] ([[Japan]]), and was a Fogarty Scholar-in-Residence at the [[National Institutes of Health]] in the [[United States]].<ref name=":0" />

His publications are widespread and well known, having had his work published in prominent journals such as the British Journal of Pharmacology and the [[Journal of Neuroscience]]. He was editor-in-chief of the [[British Journal of Pharmacology]], and served on the [[editorial board]]s of many other [[Academic journal|journals]], including the [[Journal of Physiology]], [[Neuron (journal)|Neuron]], [[Trends in Neurosciences]] and [[Proceedings of the Royal Society]].<ref name=":0" />

==Awards and honours==
Brown was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1990,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gibb |first1=Alasdair J. |last2=Smart |first2=Trevor G. |date=2025 |title=David Anthony Brown. 10 February 1936—21 October 2023 |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2024.0008 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=78 |pages=69–87 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2024.0008 |doi-access=free }}</ref> an Honorary Fellow and sometime Council Member of the [[British Pharmacological Society]], an Elected Fellow of the [[Institute of Biology]] (1980) and an Elected Fellow of [[Academia Europaea]] (1996). He won the [[Feldberg Foundation]] Prize in 1992.
